PROVEN on a real lawn with real entities: the Unity->Server HUD ingest. 21 genuine debug.actor-hud events emitted by ActorHudCache.DeltaEmit (ActorHudInvalidator.cs:49-60) and read through the Server's own /api/debug/events, plus the same nested actorHud on the census rows via ActorHudObserve.AttachRow (ids 71/79/88/89/95/96). No FE hook and no fixture were used, which is precisely what the browser-proof lane had to do. The subject is a real record, not a debug invention: the same ptr appears in stat.writer (hp 270->411, defense 0->177), debug.aptitude-trace (six real Hub subsystems) and zombie.spawn with sourceKind=creature.progression.v1 / sourceId=general:normalzombie.

ALSO PROVEN as data: element resolution on the Unity side. Real snapshots carry elements:{primary:'earth'}; earth maps to hudGlyph 'stone' in the v2 catalog this server serves; stone.png is deployed in the slot's Mods/assets/actor-hud-elements (5681B) and answers 200 image/png. The host reads the same v2 catalog (RpgHost.cs:133) as the Server (Program.cs:107-108), so the two halves agree.

ALSO PROVEN: the HUD draw switch is a real player setting and it reaches the engine. Default is off and the registry says why ('dominated vfx.tick at 2.513 ms/frame'). Flipped through the real PUT /api/settings, read back through GET /api/settings AND independently from rpg_user_settings in the DAL, and the injector visibly acted: early went world-hud-off -> idle -> ok and shaderOk False -> True. The world-hud-off value is written only at ActorHudPool.cs:127, so its appearance proves TickSync runs and its disappearance proves the push landed.

ALSO PROVEN: the HUD places slots on a live board (early=ok, hudSlots=2 with 2 live actors, ids 558/892/1050). Because _worldHud++ (ActorHudPool.cs:284) is the LAST statement of SyncEntity, reaching it means each actor cleared GetOrBuild, ShouldShow, AnchorResolver.Resolve AND ActorScreenAnchorResolver.TryResolve, and then had Root.SetActive(true) and anchoredPosition applied.

NOT PROVEN, and this is the headline: whether any of it is VISIBLE. The HUD canvas is RenderMode.ScreenSpaceOverlay (ActorHudPool.cs:395), which is composited after camera render and therefore cannot appear in a camera capture -- and the repo's own comment says the fallback 'Misses UI overlays' (ScreenshotRunner.cs:136-137). The UI-inclusive primitive needs a Repaint within 2000ms; repaintsSeen=0 on all SEVEN captures, including four after SetForegroundWindow+BringWindowToTop, and those four are byte-identical (sha256 5E774967...). So the empty-HUD screenshots are uninformative, NOT evidence of absence, and the report says so instead of claiming a green or a red.
